veranderings.voor: tot rus en bly hulle lê
veranderings.na: tot rus en bly daar lê
veranderings.rede: The repeated pronoun with inversion after 'en' reads clumsily; the shared subject carries over.

veranderings.blok: Die lae bou op en word hard
veranderings.voor: keer op keer en daar kom al hoe meer lae.
veranderings.na: keer op keer, en daar kom al hoe meer lae by.
veranderings.rede: AWS comma between two full clauses, and 'bykom' is the idiomatic verb for layers being added.

veranderings.blok: Die lae bou op en word hard
veranderings.rede: 'Vat' for duration is colloquial; 'duur' is the standard written form.

veranderings.blok: Die lae bou op en word hard
veranderings.rede: 'Lewens' alone is vague; 'menselewens' makes clear what the time is compared with.

veranderings.blok: Die strepe wat jy kan sien
veranderings.rede: AWS comma: 'en' joins two clauses that each have their own subject and verb; the protected wording after it is untouched.
'Dit' follows a sentence about 'daardie lae' and could point to the layers; naming leiklip removes the doubt.

veranderings.voor: Kalksteen is 'n gesteente wat sagter is as baie ander gesteentes.
veranderings.na: Kalksteen is sagter as baie ander gesteentes.
veranderings.rede: The relative clause is wooden and repeats 'gesteente'; the direct form says the same.
AWS comma: 'en' joins two clauses that each have their own subject and verb.
A general statement about practice reads naturally with the plural 'dakke'.
'Aanmekaarplak' is a compound verb, so its past participle is written as one word.

vlae.blok: Die lae bou op en word hard
vlae.teks: Die druk pak die korrels net stywer teen mekaar.
vlae.rede: 'Net' is ambiguous: it can mean 'only' (pressure merely packs, the cement glues) or 'even/ever tighter'; the intended reading decides the fix ('slegs' or 'nog/al hoe stywer'), so it is not changed.
